top_story: Testimony from Israeli intelligence soldiers points to an earlier shift in Gaza targeting policy that accepted civilian deaths even for low-level targets, underscoring a baseline of normalized mass harm that continues to shape Palestinian life. In the Gulf, that regional climate sharpened on 14 October when missile strikes sank two container ships near the Strait of Hormuz, directly threatening a chokepoint central to global trade and the economies that depend on it. By 15 October, the Houthis carried that escalation into Aden with a deadly strike on Yemen’s presidential palace, hitting the seat of the internationally recognized government and deepening civilian insecurity in the south. Together, the developments show a region where permissive use of force is widening from entrenched war zones into strategic maritime and political centers, increasing both humanitarian risk and the chance of broader interstate confrontation.
